title: A home network you can edit

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if your home network diagram lived in a file you could actually edit, instead of a picture nobody can change?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That sounds like every diagram I've ever lost the source for.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. This repository by Antoine keeps a home-infrastructure diagram as editable sources, in PlantUML and draw dot io, and then exports HTML and image versions.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the sources are the real thing, and the pictures come out of them?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. It's a small documentation workflow: edit the source, regenerate, and anyone can open the result without running an application. It's all under an MIT license.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Neat way to keep a home setup documented.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the idea. The repository is archived now, and the written page has the details.
